title.zh: 卷三十九 列傳第二十九 殷孝祖 劉勉
title.en: Volume 39 Biographies 29: Yin Xiaozu, Liu Mian
title.raw: 卷三十九 列傳第二十九 殷孝祖 劉勉 Volume 39 Biographies 29: Yin Xiaozu, Liu Mian

sentences.zh: 列傳第二十九

translations.literal: Biographies 29
translations.idiomatic: Biography 29

sentences.zh: 殷孝祖劉勉

translations.literal: Yin Xiaozu, Liu Mian
translations.idiomatic: Yin Xiaozu and Liu Mian

sentences.zh: 明帝初即位，四方反叛，孝祖外甥司徒參軍潁川荀僧韶建議銜命征孝祖入朝，上遣之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming had just taken the throne, the four quarters rebelled. Xiaozu's nephew, Clerk of the Masters of Writing Xun Sengshao of Yingchuan, proposed that he carry imperial orders to summon Xiaozu to court; the emperor sent him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Emperor Ming acceded, rebellions broke out on all sides. Xiaozu's nephew Xun Sengshao of Yingchuan, a clerk on the Masters of Writing staff, proposed that he be entrusted with orders summoning Xiaozu to the capital, and the emperor dispatched him.

sentences.zh: 時徐州刺史薛安都遣薛索兒等屯據津徑，僧韶間行得至，說孝祖曰：「景和凶狂，開闢未有，朝野憂危，假命漏刻。

translations.literal: At that time Xuzhou Inspector Xue Andu had sent Xue Suo'er and others to hold the ferry crossings. Sengshao went by hidden routes and arrived, and said to Xiaozu: "Jinghe was brutal and reckless beyond anything since the founding; court and countryside were gripped by dread, and the throne hung by a thread.
translations.idiomatic: The Inspector of Xuzhou, Xue Andu, had posted Xue Suo'er and others to hold the river crossings. Sengshao made his way through in secret and reached Xiaozu, saying: "The Jinghe reign was savage and reckless beyond anything since the dynasty's founding; court and countryside alike were in peril, and the throne survived only from moment to moment.

sentences.zh: 主上曾不浹辰，夷凶翦暴。

translations.literal: Our sovereign, within less than a full day, put down the villains and cut short the violence.
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign, in less than a single day, crushed the wicked and ended the violence.

sentences.zh: 國亂朝危，宜立長主，公卿百辟，人無異議。

translations.literal: With the state in turmoil and the court in crisis, it was right to establish a mature ruler; among ministers and the hundred offices, no one dissented.
translations.idiomatic: In national chaos and court crisis, a mature ruler ought to have been enthroned, and among the ministers and officials no one disagreed.

sentences.zh: 而群迷相扇，構造無端，貪利幼弱，競懷希幸。

translations.literal: Yet the deluded masses fanned one another on, fabricating groundless plots, greedy for profit from a child sovereign, each nursing vain hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the deluded stirred one another on, inventing baseless schemes, greedy for advantage from a child on the throne, each nursing empty hopes.

sentences.zh: 舅少有立功之志，長以氣節成名，若能控濟、河義勇，還奉朝廷，非唯匡主靜亂，乃可以垂名竹帛。

translations.literal: Uncle, you have long cherished the will to achieve merit and are famed for integrity; if you can rally the righteous volunteers of Ji and the Yellow River and return to serve the court, you will not only right the sovereign and pacify disorder—you may leave your name in the historical records.
translations.idiomatic: Uncle, you have cherished the will to achieve merit since youth and are famed for integrity; if you can rally the loyal volunteers along the Ji and Yellow rivers and return to serve the court, you will not only restore the sovereign and quell disorder—you may win a name that endures in the annals.

sentences.zh: 」孝祖即日棄妻子，率文武二千人隨僧韶還都。

translations.literal: That very day Xiaozu abandoned wife and children and led two thousand officers and men back to the capital with Sengshao.
translations.idiomatic: That very day Xiaozu left wife and children behind and led two thousand civil and military followers back to the capital with Sengshao.

sentences.zh: 時普天同逆，朝廷唯保丹陽一郡。

translations.literal: At the time all under Heaven shared in rebellion; the court held only Danyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the whole realm had turned rebel, and the court retained only the commandery of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 孝祖忽至，眾力不少，人情於是大安。

translations.literal: When Xiaozu arrived suddenly, his forces were no small addition, and men's hearts were greatly reassured.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozu arrived unexpectedly, his troops were a substantial reinforcement, and popular feeling was greatly reassured.

sentences.zh: 進孝祖號冠軍將軍、假節、督前鋒諸軍事。

translations.literal: Xiaozu was advanced to General Who Conquers the Champions, with credential staff, and Superintendent of Forward Armies.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozu was promoted to General Who Conquers the Champions, granted credential staff, and made superintendent of the vanguard armies.

sentences.zh: 禦仗先有諸葛亮筒袖鎧、鐵帽，二十五石弩射之不能入，上悉以賜孝祖。

translations.literal: In the imperial armory were sleeve-armors and iron caps of the kind Zhuge Liang had used; a twenty-five-stone crossbow could not pierce them—the emperor bestowed them all on Xiaozu.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial armory held sleeve-armors and iron caps said to be of Zhuge Liang's pattern; even a twenty-five-stone crossbow could not pierce them, and the emperor gave them all to Xiaozu.

sentences.zh: 孝祖負其誠節，陵轢諸將。

translations.literal: Relying on his loyal resolve, Xiaozu looked down on and insulted the other generals.
translations.idiomatic: Confident in his loyal resolve, Xiaozu treated the other generals with contempt.

sentences.zh: 時賊據赭圻，孝祖將進攻之，與大將王玄謨別，悲不自勝，眾並駭怪。

translations.literal: When the rebels held Zhixu, Xiaozu was about to attack; taking leave of the supreme commander Wang Xuemo, he could not master his grief—all were startled and baffled.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then held Zhixu, and as Xiaozu was about to advance against them he took leave of the supreme commander Wang Xuemo, overcome with grief to the point of collapse; the whole army was astonished.

sentences.zh: 泰始二年三月三日，與賊合戰，每戰，常以鼓蓋自隨。

translations.literal: On the third day of the third month of Taishi year 2, he joined battle with the enemy; in every fight he always had drum canopies follow him.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day of the third month in the second year of Taishi, he engaged the enemy in battle, and in every clash he always had drum canopies carried before him.

sentences.zh: 軍中人相謂曰：「殷統軍可謂死將矣，今與賊交鋒，而以羽儀自標顯，若射者十手攢射，欲不斃得乎。

translations.literal: Men in the army said to one another: "Commander Yin may be called a general bound for death—in combat with the enemy he marks himself with ceremonial insignia; if ten archers shot at once, how could he not be killed?"
translations.idiomatic: Men in the ranks said to one another: "Commander Yin is surely a dead man—he fights the enemy while displaying all his ceremonial banners; if ten archers loosed at once, how could he fail to fall?"

sentences.zh: 」是日中流矢死。

translations.literal: That same day he died from an arrow in flight.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he was killed by a stray arrow.

sentences.zh: 追贈建安縣侯，諡曰忠。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Jian'an; posthumous title Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Jian'an, with the posthumous title Loyal.

sentences.zh: 琰字敬瑉，孝祖族子也。

translations.literal: Yan, courtesy name Jingmin, was Xiaozu's clansman.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Yan, courtesy name Jingmin, was a clansman of Xiaozu.

sentences.zh: 父道鸞，宋衡陽王義季右軍長史。

translations.literal: His father Dao Luan was Right Army Chief Clerk to Prince Hengyang Yiji of Song.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dao Luan had served as Right Army Chief Clerk to Prince Hengyang Yiji of Song.

sentences.zh: 琰性和雅靜素，寡嗜欲，諳前世舊事。

translations.literal: Yan's nature was refined, gentle, and plain; he had few desires and was versed in affairs of past ages.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was refined, gentle, and plain by nature, with few desires, and was well versed in the affairs of earlier ages.

sentences.zh: 事兄甚謹，少以名行見稱。

translations.literal: He served his elder brother with great respect; from youth he was acclaimed for reputation and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He served his elder brother with scrupulous respect and was praised from youth for his reputation and conduct.

sentences.zh: 在壽陽被攻圍積時，為城內所懷附。

translations.literal: When Shouyang was besieged for a long time, the people within the walls attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: During the long siege of Shouyang, the people within the walls came to rely on him.

sentences.zh: 揚州刺史王景文、征西將軍蔡興宗、司空褚彥回並相與友善。

translations.literal: Yangzhou Inspector Wang Jingwen, General Who Conquers the West Cai Xingzong, and Minister of Works Chu Yanhui were all on friendly terms with him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingwen, Inspector of Yangzhou; Cai Xingzong, General Who Conquers the West; and Chu Yanhui, Minister of Works—all were on friendly terms with him.

sentences.zh: 劉勉字伯猷，彭城安上里人也。

translations.literal: Liu Mian, courtesy name Boyou, was a native of Anshang Lane in Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian, courtesy name Boyou, came from Anshang Lane in Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 祖懷義，父穎之，位並郡守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Huaiyi and father Yingzhi both held posts as commandery governors.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Huaiyi and his father Yingzhi had both served as commandery governors.

sentences.zh: 還都，拜太子右衛率，封鄱陽縣侯，遷右衛將軍，行豫州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: On returning to the capital he was appointed Right Commander of the Crown Prince's Guard, enfeoffed as Marquis of Poyang, promoted to Right Guard General, acting Inspector of Yuzhou, with overall command added.
translations.idiomatic: On his return to the capital he was appointed Right Commander of the Crown Prince's Guard, enfeoffed as Marquis of Poyang, then promoted to Right Guard General, acting Inspector of Yuzhou, with overall military authority added.

sentences.zh: 後徵拜散騎常侍、中領軍。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned and appointed Privy Attendant and Central Army Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was summoned to court and appointed Privy Attendant and Central Army Commander.

sentences.zh: 勉以世路糾紛，有懷止足，經始鍾嶺之南，以為棲息。

translations.literal: Mian, seeing the troubled times, felt the wish to know when enough was enough; south of Mount Zhong he laid out grounds for his retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the age's turmoil, Mian felt the wish to know when he had enough; south of Mount Zhong he laid out a retreat where he might rest.

sentences.zh: 聚石蓄水，髣佛丘中，朝士雅素者多往遊之。

translations.literal: He piled stones and stored water, resembling a mountain dell; many cultivated courtiers often went there to visit.
translations.idiomatic: He piled stones and stored water until the place resembled a mountain dell, and many cultivated courtiers of refined taste often came to visit.

sentences.zh: 悛字士操，隨父征竟陵王誕於廣陵，以功拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Juan, courtesy name Shicao, followed his father in campaigning against Prince Jingling Dan at Guangling and for merit was appointed Commandant of Steeds for the Palace Editor.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Juan, courtesy name Shicao, followed his father in the campaign against Prince Jingling Dan at Guangling and, for his merit, was appointed Commandant of Steeds for the Palace Editor.

sentences.zh: 後為桂陽王征北中兵參軍，與齊武帝同直殿內，並為宋明帝所親待，由是與武帝款好。

translations.literal: Later he served as Army Controller on the Northern Expedition staff of the Prince of Guiyang; he and Emperor Wu of Qi shared duty inside the palace halls, and both were treated with favor by Emperor Ming of Song—thus he and the future Emperor Wu became close friends.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as Army Controller on the Prince of Guiyang's northern campaign staff. He and the future Emperor Wu of Qi shared duty inside the palace, and both were favored by Emperor Ming of Song; from this Juan and the future emperor became intimate friends.

sentences.zh: 悛本名忱，宋明帝多忌，反語「劉忱」為「臨讎」，改名悛焉。

translations.literal: Juan's original given name was Chen; Emperor Ming of Song was much given to taboos, and the reverse reading of "Liu Chen" yielded "facing an enemy," so he renamed himself Juan.
translations.idiomatic: Juan's original given name was Chen. Emperor Ming of Song was much given to taboos, and the reverse reading of "Liu Chen" yielded "facing an enemy," so he changed his name to Juan.

sentences.zh: 齊武帝嘗至悛宅，晝臥覺，悛自捧金澡罐受四升水以沃盥，因以與帝，前後所納稱此。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Qi once came to Juan's home; Juan woke from a daytime nap and himself carried a golden bathing basin, received four sheng of water for washing, and presented it to the emperor—his earlier gifts of welcome were all on this order.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Qi once visited Juan's house. Juan woke from a midday nap, himself carried a golden bathing basin, had four sheng of water poured for washing, and presented it to the emperor; his earlier courtesies had all been of this kind.

sentences.zh: 後遷安遠護軍、武陵內史。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Protector of Pacified Distance and Internal Magistrate of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was transferred to Protector of Pacified Distance and Internal Magistrate of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 郡南古江堤久廢，悛修未畢，而江水忽至，百姓棄役奔走。

translations.literal: South of the commandery an ancient river embankment had long lain in ruins; before Juan finished repairs, the river waters suddenly rose, and the people abandoned their labor and fled.
translations.idiomatic: South of the commandery an ancient river dike had long been in ruins. Before Juan could finish repairs, the river suddenly rose, and the people abandoned their labor and fled.

sentences.zh: 悛親率厲之，於是乃立。

translations.literal: Juan personally led and urged them on, and the embankment was completed.
translations.idiomatic: Juan personally led and urged them on, and the dike was at last completed.

sentences.zh: 漢壽人邵榮興六世同爨，悛表其門閭。

translations.literal: Sha Rongxing of Hanshou had six generations eating from one hearth; Juan submitted a memorial commending his household gate.
translations.idiomatic: Sha Rongxing of Hanshou had six generations eating from a single hearth; Juan memorialized the court to honor his household.

sentences.zh: 悛強濟有世調，善於流俗。

translations.literal: Juan was forceful and resourceful, with the manners of his age, skilled in dealing with the common run of men.
translations.idiomatic: Juan was forceful and resourceful, with the manners of his generation, and skilled in dealing with the common run of society.

sentences.zh: 蠻王田僮在山中，年垂百餘歲，南譙王義宣為荊州，僮出謁，至是又謁悛。

translations.literal: The Man king Tian Tong lived in the mountains, his age nearing a hundred and more; when Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan governed Jingzhou, Tong had come to pay respects, and now did so again with Juan.
translations.idiomatic: The Man chieftain Tian Tong lived in the mountains, his age nearing a hundred. When Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan had governed Jingzhou, Tong had come to pay his respects; now he did so again to Juan.

sentences.zh: 明帝崩，表求奔赴。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming died, Juan submitted a memorial asking to hurry to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming died, Juan submitted a memorial asking leave to hurry to the capital.

sentences.zh: 敕帶郡還都，吏人送者數千萬人。

translations.literal: He was ordered to bring his commandery office back to the capital; officials and commoners who came to see him off numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to return to the capital while retaining his commandery post; officials and commoners who came to see him off numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 悛人人執手，系以涕泣，百姓感之，贈送甚厚。

translations.literal: Juan took each person's hand, tears streaming down his face; the people were moved and gave lavish parting gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Juan took each person's hand in turn, weeping as he did so; the people were deeply moved and gave lavish parting gifts.

sentences.zh: 桂陽之難，加甯朔將軍，助守石頭。

translations.literal: During the Guiyang rebellion he was given the additional title General Who Pacifies the North and assisted in defending Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guiyang rebellion he was given the additional title General Who Pacifies the North and assisted in the defense of Shitou.

sentences.zh: 父勉于大航戰死，悛時遇疾，扶伏路次，號哭求勉屍。

translations.literal: His father Mian died in battle at Dahuang; Juan was then ill, but propped himself along the roadside, wailing and begging for his father's corpse.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mian died in battle at Dahuang. Juan was then ill, yet he propped himself along the roadside, wailing and begging for his father's body.

sentences.zh: 勉屍頂後傷缺，悛割發補之。

translations.literal: On the crown of Mian's corpse the wound had left a gap; Juan cut his own hair to mend it.
translations.idiomatic: A gap had been torn in the crown of Mian's skull where he was wounded; Juan cut his own hair to fill it.

sentences.zh: 持喪墓側，冬日不衣絮。

translations.literal: He kept mourning beside the tomb, and in winter wore no cotton padding.
translations.idiomatic: He kept vigil mourning beside the tomb and in winter wore no quilted garments.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝代勉為領軍，素與勉善，書譬悛殷勤抑勉。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao of Qi replaced Mian as Army Commander; he had long been on good terms with Mian and wrote to Juan with earnest words of consolation and restraint on mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao of Qi replaced Mian as Army Commander. He had long been on good terms with Mian and wrote to Juan with earnest words urging him to moderate his grief.

sentences.zh: 建平王景素反，高帝總眾。

translations.literal: When Prince of Jianping Jingsu rebelled, Emperor Gao took command of all forces.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jianping Jingsu rebelled, Emperor Gao took overall command of the armies.

sentences.zh: 悛初免喪，高帝召悛及弟愃入省，欲使領支軍。

translations.literal: Juan had just left mourning; Emperor Gao summoned Juan and his younger brother Juan into the palace, intending to put them in charge of a support army.
translations.idiomatic: Juan had just ended his mourning period. Emperor Gao summoned Juan and his younger brother Quan into the palace, intending to put them in command of a support army.

sentences.zh: 及見皆羸削改貌，乃止。

translations.literal: When he saw them both emaciated and altered in appearance, he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw them both wasted and altered beyond recognition, he abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 霸業初建，悛先致誠節，沈攸之事起，加輔國將軍。

translations.literal: When the great enterprise was first being founded, Juan was first to show loyal resolve; when Shen Youzhi's affair broke out, he was made General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: As the new dynasty's enterprise was first taking shape, Juan was among the first to show loyal resolve. When Shen Youzhi's rebellion broke out, he was made General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 後為廣州刺史，襲爵鄱陽縣侯。

translations.literal: Later he became Inspector of Guangzhou and inherited the marquisate of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became Inspector of Guangzhou and inherited the marquisate of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 武帝自尋陽還，遇悛，歡宴敘舊，停十餘日乃下。

translations.literal: The Emperor Wu returning from Xunyang met Juan; they feasted in joy and recalled old times, and he lingered more than ten days before leaving.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from Xunyang, Emperor Wu met Juan; they feasted in joy and recalled old times, and the emperor lingered more than ten days before departing.

sentences.zh: 遣文惠太子及竟陵王子良攝衣履，備父友之敬。

translations.literal: He sent Crown Prince Wenhu and Prince of Jingling Ziliang to adjust their dress and shoes and show the respect due a father's friend.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Crown Prince Wenhu and Prince Jingling Ziliang to straighten their dress and shoes and show the respect due a father's friend.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，國除，平西記室參軍夏侯恭叔上書，以柳元景中興功臣，劉勉殞身王事，宜存封爵。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, the state [of Song's grants] was abolished; Army Controller on the Pacified West staff Xia Hou Gongshu submitted a memorial arguing that Liu Yuanyijing was a meritorious minister of the restoration and Liu Mian gave his life in the royal service—their enfeoffments ought to be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, the Song state was abolished. Xia Hou Gongshu, Army Controller on the Pacified West staff, submitted a memorial arguing that Liu Yuanyijing had been a meritorious minister of the restoration and Liu Mian had given his life in royal service—their enfeoffments ought to be preserved.

sentences.zh: 詔以與運隆替，不容復厝意也。

translations.literal: An edict replied that as dynasties rise and fall in succession, no further attention could be given to the matter.
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied that as dynasties rose and fell in turn, no further heed could be paid to the matter.

sentences.zh: 初，蒼梧廢，高帝集議中華門，見悛謂曰：「君昨直邪？

translations.literal: Earlier, when [Emperor] Cangwu was deposed, Emperor Gao assembled counsel at the Zhonghua Gate; seeing Juan he said: "Were you upright yesterday?"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Emperor Cangwu was deposed, Emperor Gao assembled counsel at the Zhonghua Gate. Seeing Juan, he said: "Were you upright yesterday?"

sentences.zh: 「悛曰：「僕昨正直，而之急在外。

translations.literal: Juan said: "Your servant was upright yesterday, but Your Majesty's urgency lay elsewhere."
translations.idiomatic: Juan said: "Your servant was upright yesterday, but Your Majesty's urgency lay elsewhere."

sentences.zh: 」至是，上謂悛曰：「功名之際，人所不忘，卿昔在中華門答我，何其欲謝世事？

translations.literal: At this time the emperor said to Juan: "At moments of glory and reward, people do not forget—when you answered me at Zhonghua Gate, how keen you seemed to withdraw from worldly affairs!"
translations.idiomatic: At this point the emperor said to Juan: "At moments of glory and reward, people do not forget. When you answered me at the Zhonghua Gate, how eager you seemed to withdraw from worldly affairs!"

sentences.zh: 」悛曰：「臣世受宋恩，門荷齊眷，非常之勳，非臣所及，敢不以實仰答。」

translations.literal: Juan said: "Your servant's house received Song's grace for generations and now bears Qi's favor; extraordinary merit is beyond me—I would not dare answer otherwise than truthfully."
translations.idiomatic: Juan said: "Your servant's house received Song's grace for generations and now bears Qi's favor. Extraordinary merit is beyond me—I would not dare answer otherwise than truthfully."

sentences.zh: 遷太子中庶子，領越騎校尉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Attendant to the Crown Prince and concurrently made Commandant of the Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Palace Attendant to the Crown Prince and concurrently made Commandant of the Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 時武帝在東宮，每幸悛坊，閑言至夕，賜屏風帷帳。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Wu was in the Eastern Palace; he often visited Juan's quarters, conversing at leisure until evening, and bestowed screens and curtains.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the future Emperor Wu was in the Eastern Palace; he often visited Juan's quarters, talking at leisure until evening, and bestowed screens and curtains.

sentences.zh: 武帝即位，改領前軍將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Juan was changed to command the Forward Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Juan was made to command the Forward Army in addition to his other posts.

sentences.zh: 後拜司州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Inspector of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Inspector of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 悛父勉討殷琰，平壽陽，無所犯害，百姓德之，為罍樽、銅豆、鍾各二口獻之。

translations.literal: Juan's father Mian had campaigned against Yin Yan, pacified Shouyang, and harmed no one; the people were grateful and presented two each of wine jars, bronze dou vessels, and bells.
translations.idiomatic: Juan's father Mian had campaigned against Yin Yan, pacified Shouyang, and harmed no one; the people were grateful and presented two each of wine jars, bronze dou vessels, and bells as gifts.

sentences.zh: 遷長兼侍中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve concurrently as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve concurrently as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 車駕數幸悛宅。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage often visited Juan's home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often visited Juan's home in person.

sentences.zh: 宅盛修山池，造甕牖。

translations.literal: The residence was lavishly furnished with hills and pools; he built jar-windows.
translations.idiomatic: The residence was lavishly laid out with hills and pools, and he built jar-shaped windows.

sentences.zh: 武帝著鹿皮冠，披悛菟皮衾，於牖中宴樂。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu wore a deerskin cap and wrapped himself in Juan's rabbit-fur quilt; they feasted and made merry in the windowed alcove.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu wore a deerskin cap and wrapped himself in Juan's rabbit-fur quilt; they feasted and made merry in the jar-window alcove.

sentences.zh: 以冠賜悛，至夜乃去。

translations.literal: He gave the cap to Juan and did not leave until night.
translations.idiomatic: He gave the cap to Juan and did not leave until nightfall.

sentences.zh: 後從駕登蔣山，上數歎曰：「貧賤之交不可忘，糟糠之妻不下堂。

translations.literal: Later, following the imperial progress up Mount Jiang, the emperor sighed repeatedly: "Friendship in poverty and low estate must not be forgotten; the wife who shared one's chaff and husks does not leave the hall."
translations.idiomatic: Later, accompanying the emperor up Mount Jiang, the sovereign sighed repeatedly: "Friendship in poverty and low estate must not be forgotten; the wife who shared one's chaff and husks does not leave the hall."

sentences.zh: 」顧謂悛曰：「此況卿也。

translations.literal: Turning to Juan he said: "This applies to you."
translations.idiomatic: Turning to Juan he said: "That is how it is with you."

sentences.zh: 世言富貴好改其素情，吾雖有四海，今日與卿盡布衣之適。

translations.literal: The world says that wealth and rank make one change one's former feelings; though I possess the four seas, today with you I enjoy the ease of plain cloth.
translations.idiomatic: People say that wealth and rank make one change one's former feelings. Though I possess the four seas, today with you I enjoy the ease of old friends in plain cloth.

sentences.zh: 」悛起拜謝。

translations.literal: Juan rose and bowed in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Juan rose and bowed in thanks.

sentences.zh: 累遷始興王前軍長史、平蠻校尉、蜀郡太守，行益州府州事。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Forward Army Chief Clerk on the staff of the Prince of Shixing, Commandant Who Pacifies the Man, and Administrator of Shujun, acting on the affairs of the Yizhou headquarters and province.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Forward Army Chief Clerk on the staff of the Prince of Shixing, Commandant Who Pacifies the Man, and Administrator of Shujun, with authority over the Yizhou headquarters and provincial affairs.

sentences.zh: 初，高帝輔政，有意欲鑄錢，以禪讓之際，未及施行。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Gao was regent, he had intended to cast coin, but at the time of the abdication he had not yet carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Emperor Gao was regent, he had intended to cast new coin, but at the moment of the abdication he had not yet carried the plan out.

sentences.zh: 建

translations.literal: Jian
translations.idiomatic: Jian

sentences.zh: 元四年，奉朝請孔覬上鑄錢均貨議，辭證甚博，其略以為：食貨相通，理勢自然。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuan, Court Gentleman Kong Guan submitted a memorial on casting coin and equalizing goods; his argument was very broad, and in summary he held that food and goods must circulate—this is the natural order of reason and circumstance.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jianyuan, Court Gentleman Kong Guan submitted a memorial on casting coin and equalizing goods; his argument was very broad. In summary he held that food and goods must circulate—this follows naturally from reason and circumstance.

sentences.zh: 李悝曰：「糴甚貴傷人，甚賤傷農。

translations.literal: Li Kui said: "When grain is bought very dear, it harms the people; when very cheap, it harms the farmers."
translations.idiomatic: Li Kui said: "When grain is bought very dear, it harms the people; when very cheap, it harms the farmers."

sentences.zh: 人傷則離散，農傷則國貧。

translations.literal: When the people are harmed, they scatter; when the farmers are harmed, the state is poor.
translations.idiomatic: When the people are harmed, they scatter; when the farmers are harmed, the state grows poor.

sentences.zh: 甚賤與甚貴，其傷一也。

translations.literal: Extreme cheapness and extreme dearness do equal harm.
translations.idiomatic: Extreme cheapness and extreme dearness do equal harm.

sentences.zh: 」三吳國之關奧，比歲時被水潦，而糴不貴，是天下錢少，非穀穰賤，此不可不察也。

translations.literal: The Three Wu region is the vital center of the state; in recent years it has suffered floods, yet grain is not dear—this shows that coin in the realm is scarce, not that grain is abundant and cheap; this must not go unexamined.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Wu region is the vital center of the state. In recent years it has suffered floods, yet grain is not dear—this shows that coin in the realm is scarce, not that grain is abundant and cheap. This must not go unexamined.

sentences.zh: 鑄錢之弊，在輕重屢變。

translations.literal: The harm in casting coin lies in the repeated changes of weight.
translations.idiomatic: The harm in casting coin lies in the repeated changes of weight.

sentences.zh: 重錢患難用，而難用為累輕；

translations.literal: Heavy coin is troubled by difficulty of use, and difficulty of use becomes a pressure toward lightness;
translations.idiomatic: Heavy coin is troubled by difficulty of use, and difficulty of use becomes a pressure toward lightness;

sentences.zh: 輕錢弊盜鑄，而盜鑄為禍深。

translations.literal: light coin is harmed by illicit casting, and illicit casting brings deep calamity.
translations.idiomatic: light coin is harmed by illicit casting, and illicit casting brings deep calamity.

sentences.zh: 人所盜鑄，嚴法不禁者，由上鑄錢惜銅愛工也。

translations.literal: That people illicitly cast coin despite severe laws unchecked is because the state, in casting coin, spares copper and prizes labor.
translations.idiomatic: That people illicitly cast coin despite severe laws is because the state, in its own coinage, spares copper and prizes labor.

sentences.zh: 惜銅愛工，謂錢無用之器，以通交易，務欲令輕而數多，使省工而易成，不詳慮其為患也。

translations.literal: Sparing copper and prizing labor means treating coin as a useless vessel merely to facilitate exchange, striving to make it light and numerous, saving labor and making it easy to produce, without fully considering the harm.
translations.idiomatic: Sparing copper and prizing labor means treating coin as a mere instrument of exchange, striving to make it light and numerous, saving labor and making it easy to produce, without fully weighing the harm.

sentences.zh: 自漢鑄五銖至宋文帝，曆五百餘年，制度世有廢興，而不變五銖錢者，明其輕重可法，得貨之宜。

translations.literal: From Han's casting of the five-zhu coin to Emperor Wen of Song, more than five hundred years passed; institutions rose and fell with the ages, yet the five-zhu coin was not changed—showing that its weight could serve as law and its value suited circulation.
translations.idiomatic: From the Han casting of the five-zhu coin to Emperor Wen of Song, more than five hundred years passed. Institutions rose and fell with the ages, yet the five-zhu coin was not changed—showing that its weight could serve as a standard and its value suited circulation.

sentences.zh: 以為宜開置泉府，方牧貢金，大興鎔鑄。

translations.literal: He held that it was fitting to establish a treasury for coin, have the regional inspectors present gold as tribute, and greatly expand casting.
translations.idiomatic: He held that it was fitting to establish a treasury for coin, have the regional inspectors present gold as tribute, and greatly expand casting.

sentences.zh: 錢重五銖，一依漢法。

translations.literal: Coin should weigh five zhu, following the Han standard in all respects.
translations.idiomatic: Coin should weigh five zhu, following the Han standard in all respects.

sentences.zh: 若官鑄已布於人，便嚴斷翦鑿，輕小破缺無周郭者，悉不得行。

translations.literal: Once official coin had been distributed among the people, clipping and chiseling should be strictly forbidden; light, small, broken, or rimless pieces should none be allowed to circulate.
translations.idiomatic: Once official coin had been distributed among the people, clipping and chiseling were to be strictly forbidden; light, small, broken, or rimless pieces were none to be allowed in circulation.

sentences.zh: 官錢細小者，稱合銖兩，銷以為大。

translations.literal: Official coin that was too small should be weighed to the zhu and liang standard and melted down to make large pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Official coin that was too small should be weighed to the zhu and liang standard and melted down to make large pieces.

sentences.zh: 利貧良之人，塞奸巧之路。

translations.literal: This would benefit the poor and honest and block the path of the crafty.
translations.idiomatic: This would benefit the poor and honest and block the path of the crafty.

sentences.zh: 錢貨既均，遠近若一，百姓樂業，市道無爭，衣食滋殖矣。

translations.literal: Once coin and goods were equalized, near and far would be as one; the people would rejoice in their occupations, markets would be without contention, and food and clothing would increase.
translations.idiomatic: Once coin and goods were equalized, near and far would be as one; the people would rejoice in their occupations, markets would be without contention, and food and clothing would flourish.

sentences.zh: 時議多以錢貨輕轉少，宜更廣鑄，重其銖兩，以防人奸。

translations.literal: At the time many in debate held that coin was light and scarce and that casting should be expanded and the zhu weight increased to guard against human fraud.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many held that coin was light and scarce, and that casting should be expanded and the weight increased to guard against fraud.

sentences.zh: 高帝使諸州郡大市銅炭，會晏駕事寢。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao ordered the provinces and commanderies to market copper and charcoal on a large scale, but when he died suddenly the matter lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao ordered the provinces and commanderies to procure copper and charcoal on a large scale, but when he died suddenly the matter lapsed.

sentences.zh: 永明八年，悛啟武帝曰：「南廣郡界蒙山下有城名蒙城，可二頃地，有燒爐四所，高一丈，廣一丈五尺。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongming, Juan reported to Emperor Wu: "Within the bounds of Nanguang commandery, below Mount Meng, is a town called Mengcheng, about two qing of land, with four smelting furnaces, one zhang high and one zhang five chi wide.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yongming, Juan reported to Emperor Wu: "Within the bounds of Nanguang commandery, below Mount Meng, is a town called Mengcheng, covering about two qing of land, with four smelting furnaces, each one zhang high and one zhang five chi wide.

sentences.zh: 從蒙城度水南百許步，平地掘土深二尺，得銅。

translations.literal: From Mengcheng, crossing the water south about a hundred paces, if one digs two chi deep in level ground, one obtains copper.
translations.idiomatic: From Mengcheng, crossing the water about a hundred paces to the south, if one digs two chi deep in level ground, one finds copper.

sentences.zh: 又有古掘銅坑深二丈，並居宅處猶存。

translations.literal: There were also ancient copper pits dug two zhang deep, and the sites of dwellings still remained.
translations.idiomatic: There were also ancient copper pits dug two zhang deep, and the sites of former dwellings still remained.

sentences.zh: 鄧通南安人，漢文帝賜通嚴道縣銅山鑄錢。

translations.literal: Deng Tong was a native of Nan'an; Emperor Wen of Han granted Tong the copper mountain of Yandao county to cast coin.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Tong was a native of Nan'an. Emperor Wen of Han granted him the copper mountain in Yandao county to cast coin.

sentences.zh: 今蒙山近在青衣水南，青衣左側並是故秦之嚴道地。

translations.literal: Now Mount Meng lies close south of the Qingyi River; the left bank of Qingyi was all the old Qin territory of Yandao.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Meng now lies just south of the Qingyi River, and the left bank of Qingyi was all the old Qin territory of Yandao.

sentences.zh: 青衣縣，文帝改名漢嘉。

translations.literal: Qingyi county—Emperor Wen renamed it Hanjia.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyi county had been renamed Hanjia by Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 且蒙山去南安二百里，案此必是通所鑄處。

translations.literal: Moreover Mount Meng is two hundred li from Nan'an; by this evidence it must be where Tong cast coin.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Mount Meng is two hundred li from Nan'an; on this evidence it must be where Tong cast coin.

sentences.zh: 近喚蒙山獠出，雲'甚可經略'。

translations.literal: Recently the Liao of Mount Meng were summoned forth; they said it was very suitable for development.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the tribal people of Mount Meng were summoned forth; they said the place was very suitable for development.

sentences.zh: 此議若立，潤利無極。

translations.literal: If this proposal were adopted, profit would be boundless.
translations.idiomatic: If this proposal were adopted, the profit would be boundless.

sentences.zh: 並獻蒙山銅一片，又銅石一片，平州鑄鐵刀一口。

translations.literal: He also presented a piece of Mount Meng copper, another piece of copper ore, and an iron knife cast in Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He also presented one piece of Mount Meng copper, one piece of copper ore, and an iron knife cast in Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 」上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 遣使入蜀鑄錢，得千餘萬，功費多乃止。

translations.literal: He sent envoys into Shu to cast coin and obtained more than ten million, but because costs were high he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys into Shu to cast coin and obtained more than ten million pieces, but because the costs were high he abandoned the project.

sentences.zh: 悛仍代始興王鑒為益州刺史、監益甯二州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Juan then replaced Prince Shixing Jian as Inspector of Yizhou and overseer of military affairs in Yizhou and Ningzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Juan then replaced Prince Shixing Jian as Inspector of Yizhou and military overseer of Yizhou and Ningzhou.

sentences.zh: 悛既藉舊恩，尤能承迎權貴，賓客閨房，供費奢廣。

translations.literal: Juan, relying on old favor, was especially able to court the powerful; guests and inner chambers alike were supplied at lavish expense.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on his old favor with the throne, Juan was especially skilled at courting the powerful; guests and household alike were maintained at lavish expense.

sentences.zh: 罷廣、司二州，傾資貢獻，家無留儲。

translations.literal: On leaving Guangzhou and Sizhou he poured out his wealth in tribute; the family kept no reserves.
translations.idiomatic: On leaving his posts in Guangzhou and Sizhou he poured out his wealth in tribute gifts, until the family kept no reserves.

sentences.zh: 在蜀作金浴盆，余金物稱是。

translations.literal: In Shu he made a golden bathing basin, and other gold objects in proportion.
translations.idiomatic: In Shu he had a golden bathing basin made, with other gold objects in proportion.

sentences.zh: 罷任以本號還都，欲獻之，而武帝晏駕。

translations.literal: On leaving office he returned to the capital with his former title, intending to present them, but Emperor Wu died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: On leaving office he returned to the capital with his former title, intending to present the gifts, but Emperor Wu died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 郁林新立，悛奉獻減少。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yulin was newly enthroned, Juan's tribute was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yulin was newly enthroned, Juan offered a reduced tribute.

sentences.zh: 郁林知之，諷有司收悛付廷尉，將加誅戮。

translations.literal: Yulin learned of it and hinted that the authorities should arrest Juan and hand him to the Minister of Justice for execution.
translations.idiomatic: Yulin learned of it and hinted that the authorities should arrest Juan, hand him to the Minister of Justice, and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 明帝啟救之，見原，禁錮終身。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming intervened to save him; he was pardoned but confined for life.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming intervened to save him; he was pardoned but confined for life.

sentences.zh: 雖見廢黜，而賓客日至。

translations.literal: Though dismissed and disgraced, guests came daily.
translations.idiomatic: Though dismissed and disgraced, guests still came daily.

sentences.zh: 子孺字季幼，幼聰敏，七歲能屬文。

translations.literal: His son Ru, courtesy name Jiyou, was clever from childhood and at seven could compose prose.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liu Ru, courtesy name Jiyou, was clever from childhood and at seven could compose prose.

sentences.zh: 年十四居喪，毀瘠骨立，宗黨咸異之。

translations.literal: At fourteen he kept mourning; wasted to the bone, all his clan marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he kept mourning for a parent, wasted to skin and bone, and all his clan marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 叔父瑱為義興郡，攜以之官，常置坐側，謂賓客曰：「此吾家明珠也。

translations.literal: His uncle Zhen was magistrate of Yixing and took him to his post, always seating him at his side; he told guests: "This is the bright pearl of our house."
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Zhen was magistrate of Yixing and took him to his post, always seating him at his side. He told guests: "This is the bright pearl of our house."

sentences.zh: 」及長，美風采，性通和，雖家人不見其喜慍。

translations.literal: When grown, he had fine bearing; his nature was open and harmonious—even family never saw him show joy or anger.
translations.idiomatic: When grown, he had a fine bearing and an open, harmonious nature—even his family never saw him show joy or anger.

sentences.zh: 本州召迎主簿。

translations.literal: His home province summoned him as Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: His home province summoned him to serve as Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 起家中軍法曹行參軍，時鎮軍沈約聞其名，引為主簿，恒與遊宴賦詩，大為約所嗟賞。

translations.literal: He entered office as Acting Army Controller in the Central Army Legal Bureau; at the time General Who Pacifies the Army Shen Yue heard his name and took him as Chief Clerk, often feasting and composing poetry with him—greatly admired by Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office as Acting Army Controller in the Central Army Legal Bureau. Shen Yue, General Who Pacifies the Army, heard his name and took him as Chief Clerk; they often feasted and composed poetry together, and Yue greatly admired him.

sentences.zh: 累遷太子中舍人。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Attendant in the Crown Prince's household.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Attendant in the Crown Prince's household.

sentences.zh: 孺少好文章，性又敏速，嘗在御坐為李賦，受詔便成，文不加點。

translations.literal: Ru from youth loved literature and was quick by nature; once in the imperial presence he composed a rhapsody on plums—on receiving the edict he finished at once, the text needing no correction.
translations.idiomatic: Ru had loved literature from youth and was quick by nature. Once in the imperial presence he composed a rhapsody on plums; on receiving the command he finished at once, the text needing no correction.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝甚稱賞之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang greatly praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang greatly praised and rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 後侍宴壽光殿，詔群臣賦詩。

translations.literal: Later, attending a feast in the Shouguang Hall, the emperor ordered the ministers to compose poems.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at a feast in the Shouguang Hall, the emperor ordered the ministers to compose poems.

sentences.zh: 時孺與張率並醉，未及成。

translations.literal: At the time Ru and Zhang Shuai were both drunk and had not finished in time.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Ru and Zhang Shuai were both drunk and had not finished in time.

sentences.zh: 帝取孺手板題戲之曰：「張率東南美，劉孺洛陽才，攬筆便應就，何事久遲回。

translations.literal: The emperor took Ru's writing tablet and inscribed in jest: "Zhang Shuai, southern beauty of the east; Liu Ru, Luoyang talent—take up the brush and it should be done; why linger so long?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took Ru's writing tablet and inscribed in jest: "Zhang Shuai, southern beauty of the east; Liu Ru, Luoyang talent—take up the brush and it should be done at once; why linger so long?"

sentences.zh: 」其見親愛如此。

translations.literal: Such was the affection in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the affection in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 遷中書郎，兼中書通事舍人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Secretariat Gentleman and concurrently made Secretariat Attendant for Current Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Secretariat Gentleman and concurrently made Secretariat Attendant for Current Affairs.

sentences.zh: 曆太子中庶子，尚書吏部郎。

translations.literal: He served as Palace Attendant to the Crown Prince and Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Palace Attendant to the Crown Prince and Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 累遷散騎常侍，左戶尚書。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Privy Attendant and Minister of the Left Household.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Privy Attendant and Minister of the Left Household.

sentences.zh: 大同五年，守吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Datong he held acting appointment as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Datong he served as acting Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 出為晉陵太守，在郡和理，為吏人所稱。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Jinling; in the commandery he was harmonious and orderly, praised by officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Administrator of Jinling; in the commandery he governed harmoniously and was praised by officials and people alike.

sentences.zh: 入為侍中。

translations.literal: He entered court as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 後復為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Later he again became Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Later he again became Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 母憂，以毀卒，諡曰孝子。

translations.literal: In mourning for his mother he died from grief; his posthumous title was Filial Son.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning for his mother he died from grief; he was given the posthumous title Filial Son.

sentences.zh: 孺少與從兄苞、孝綽齊名，苞早卒，孝綽數坐免黜，位並不高，唯孺貴顯。

translations.literal: Ru from youth was famed alongside his cousins Bao and Xiaochuo; Bao died early, Xiaochuo was repeatedly dismissed for offenses, and their ranks were not high—only Ru rose to glory.
translations.idiomatic: Ru had been famed from youth alongside his cousins Bao and Xiaochuo. Bao died early; Xiaochuo was repeatedly dismissed for offenses and neither rose high—only Ru attained eminence.

sentences.zh: 有文集二十卷。

translations.literal: He left a collected works in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected works in twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 孺弟覽。

translations.literal: Ru's younger brother Lan.
translations.idiomatic: Ru's younger brother was Liu Lan.

sentences.zh: 覽字孝智，十六通老、易，位中書郎。

translations.literal: Lan, courtesy name Xiaozhi, at sixteen mastered the Laozi and Changes; he reached the post of Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lan, courtesy name Xiaozhi, at sixteen had mastered the Laozi and the Book of Changes; he rose to Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 以所生母憂，廬於墓，再期不嚐鹽酪，食麥粥而已。

translations.literal: In mourning for his birth mother he built a hut at the tomb; for two years he tasted no salt or dairy, eating only barley gruel.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning for his birth mother he built a hut at the tomb; for two years he tasted no salt or dairy and ate only barley gruel.

sentences.zh: 隆冬止著單布衣，家人慮不勝喪，中夜竊置炭於床下，覽因暖得寐。

translations.literal: In deep winter he wore only a single layer of cloth; his family feared he could not endure the mourning, and in the middle of the night secretly placed charcoal under his bed—Lan slept from the warmth.
translations.idiomatic: In deep winter he wore only a single layer of cloth. His family feared he could not endure the mourning and in the middle of the night secretly placed charcoal under his bed; Lan slept from the warmth.

sentences.zh: 及覺知之，號慟歐血。

translations.literal: When he woke and knew, he wailed in anguish and vomited blood.
translations.idiomatic: When he woke and discovered it, he wailed in anguish and vomited blood.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝聞其至性，數使省視。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang heard of his supreme filiality and repeatedly sent men to visit and check on him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang heard of his supreme filial devotion and repeatedly sent men to visit and check on him.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除尚書左丞。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was appointed Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 性聰敏，尚書令史七百人，一見並記名姓。

translations.literal: By nature clever, among seven hundred clerks of the Masters of Writing he remembered every name on a single meeting.
translations.idiomatic: Clever by nature, among the seven hundred clerks of the Masters of Writing he remembered every name after a single meeting.

sentences.zh: 當官清正無所私。

translations.literal: In office he was upright and without partiality.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was upright and without partiality.

sentences.zh: 從兄吏部郎孝綽，在職頗通贓貨，覽劾奏免官。

translations.literal: His cousin Xiaochuo, Director in the Ministry of Personnel, while in office was much involved in bribes; Lan impeached him and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Xiaochuo, Director in the Ministry of Personnel, while in office was much involved in bribes; Lan impeached him and had him dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 孝綽怨之，常謂人曰：「犬噬行路，覽噬家人。

translations.literal: Xiaochuo resented him and often told people: "A dog bites passersby; Lan bites his own kin."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaochuo resented him and often said: "A dog bites passersby; Lan bites his own kin."

sentences.zh: 」出為始興內史，居郡尤勵清節。

translations.literal: He went out as Internal Magistrate of Shixing and in the commandery especially upheld pure conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Internal Magistrate of Shixing and in the commandery especially upheld pure conduct.

sentences.zh: 復為左丞，卒官。

translations.literal: He again became Left Assistant Director and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He again became Left Assistant Director and died in office.

sentences.zh: 覽弟遵。

translations.literal: Lan's younger brother Zun.
translations.idiomatic: Lan's younger brother was Liu Zun.

sentences.zh: 遵字孝陵，少清雅有學行，工屬文。

translations.literal: Zun, courtesy name Xiaoling, from youth was refined and elegant, with learning and conduct, skilled at composition.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zun, courtesy name Xiaoling, was refined and elegant from youth, with learning and conduct, and skilled at composition.

sentences.zh: 為晉安王綱宣惠、雲麾二府記室，甚見賓禮。

translations.literal: He served as Recorder on the staffs of Prince Jin'an Gang's Xuanhui and Cloud Banner offices, greatly honored as a guest.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Recorder on the staffs of Prince Jin'an Gang's Xuanhui and Cloud Banner offices and was greatly honored as a guest.

sentences.zh: 王立為皇太子，仍除中庶子。

translations.literal: When the prince was established as crown prince, Zun was appointed Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince was established as crown prince, Zun was appointed Palace Attendant to him.

sentences.zh: 遵自隨蕃及在東宮，以舊恩偏蒙寵遇，時輩莫及。

translations.literal: Zun from following the prince in his fief through service in the Eastern Palace, by old favor received special favor—none of his contemporaries could match it.
translations.idiomatic: From following the prince in his fief through service in the Eastern Palace, Zun by old favor received special treatment—none of his contemporaries could match it.

sentences.zh: 卒官，皇太子深悼惜之，與遵從兄陽羨令孝儀令曰：「賢從弟中庶奄至殞逝，痛可言乎。

translations.literal: He died in office; the crown prince deeply mourned him and sent a message to Zun's cousin Xiaoyi, Magistrate of Yangxian: "Your worthy cousin the Palace Attendant has suddenly perished—can words express the pain?"
translations.idiomatic: He died in office. The crown prince deeply mourned him and sent a message to Zun's cousin Xiaoyi, Magistrate of Yangxian: "Your worthy cousin the Palace Attendant has suddenly perished—can words express the pain?"

sentences.zh: 其孝友淳深，立身貞固，內含玉潤，外表瀾清，言行相符，終始如一。

translations.literal: His filial piety and brotherly love were pure and deep; his conduct was steadfast; within he held jade's luster, without he showed the clear tide; words and deeds matched, beginning and end were one.
translations.idiomatic: His filial piety and brotherly love were pure and deep; his conduct was steadfast; within he held jade's luster, without he showed clear waters; words and deeds matched, and beginning and end were one.

sentences.zh: 文史該富，琬琰為心，辭章博贍，玄黃成采。

translations.literal: His letters and histories were comprehensive; fine jade was his heart; his literary compositions were broad and rich, black and yellow forming their hues.
translations.idiomatic: His command of letters and histories was comprehensive; fine jade was his heart; his literary compositions were broad and rich, woven of many hues.

sentences.zh: 既以鳴謙表性，又以難進自居。

translations.literal: He both expressed his nature through modest renown and held himself aloof from easy advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He both expressed his nature through modest renown and held himself aloof from easy advancement.

sentences.zh: 吾昔在漢南，連翩書記；

translations.literal: I once was in the Han south, with you constantly at my side as recorder;
translations.idiomatic: I once was in the Han south, with you constantly at my side as recorder;

sentences.zh: 及忝朱方，從容坐首。

translations.literal: and when I held Zhufang, you sat at ease in the foremost place.
translations.idiomatic: and when I held Zhufang, you sat at ease in the foremost place.

sentences.zh: 鷁舟乍動，朱鷺徐鳴，未嘗一日而不追隨，一時而不會遇。

translations.literal: When the egret-prowed boat stirred or the vermilion heron sounded slowly, not a day passed without your following, not a moment without our meeting.
translations.idiomatic: When the egret-prowed boat stirred or the vermilion heron sounded slowly, there was not a day without your following me, not a moment without our meeting.

sentences.zh: 益者三友，此實其人。

translations.literal: Of the three friends who bring benefit, this was truly such a man.
translations.idiomatic: Of the three friends who bring benefit, this was truly such a man.

sentences.zh: 及弘道下邑，未申善政，而能使人結去思，野多馴翟，此亦威鳳一羽，足以驗其五德。

translations.literal: When he spread the Way in a humble town, though he had not yet fully enacted good government, he could make people on departing tie up tokens of longing, and in the fields many tame pheasants appeared—this too, like one feather of the majestic phoenix, was enough to verify his five virtues.
translations.idiomatic: When he spread the Way in a humble town, though he had not yet fully enacted good government, he could make people on departing tie tokens of longing, and tame pheasants filled the fields—like one feather of the majestic phoenix, enough to show his five virtues.

sentences.zh: 」其見愛賞如此。

translations.literal: Such was the love and esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the love and esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 苞字孝嘗，一字孟嘗，悛弟子也。

translations.literal: Bao, courtesy name Xiaochang, also styled Mengchang, was Juan's nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bao, courtesy name Xiaochang, also styled Mengchang, was Juan's nephew.

sentences.zh: 父愃，位太子中庶子。

translations.literal: His father Quan held the post of Palace Attendant to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: His father Quan had served as Palace Attendant to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 苞三歲而孤，至六七歲，見諸父常泣。

translations.literal: Bao was orphaned at three; by six or seven, when he saw his uncles he often wept.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was orphaned at three; by six or seven, whenever he saw his uncles he often wept.

sentences.zh: 時伯叔父悛、繪等並顯貴，其母謂其畏憚，怒之。

translations.literal: At the time his uncles Juan, Hui, and others were all eminent; his mother thought he feared them and grew angry.
translations.idiomatic: At the time his uncles Juan, Hui, and others were all eminent; his mother thought he feared them and grew angry.

sentences.zh: 苞曰：「早孤不及有識，聞諸父多相似，故心中悲耳。

translations.literal: Bao said: "Orphaned early, I never knew them while conscious; hearing that my uncles greatly resemble one another, I grieve in my heart—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Bao said: "Orphaned early, I never knew them while I could understand; hearing that my uncles greatly resemble one another, I grieve in my heart—that is all."

sentences.zh: 」因而歔欷，母亦悲慟。

translations.literal: He then sighed and wept, and his mother too was stricken with grief.
translations.idiomatic: He then sighed and wept, and his mother too was stricken with grief.

sentences.zh: 初，苞父母及兩兄相繼亡歿，悉假瘞焉。

translations.literal: Earlier, Bao's parents and two elder brothers had died in succession, all provisionally interred.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Bao's parents and two elder brothers had died in succession and were all provisionally interred.

sentences.zh: 苞年十六，始移墓所，經營改葬，不資諸父。

translations.literal: At sixteen Bao first moved the gravesites and arranged reburial without relying on his uncles.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen Bao first moved the gravesites and arranged reburial without relying on his uncles.

sentences.zh: 奉君母朱夫人及所生陳氏並扇席溫枕，叔父繪常歎伏之。

translations.literal: He served his stepmother Lady Zhu and his birth mother Lady Chen with fanning the bed and warming the pillow; his uncle Hui often sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: He fanned the bed and warmed the pillow for his stepmother Lady Zhu and his birth mother Lady Chen alike; his uncle Hui often sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 少好學，能屬文，家有舊書，例皆殘蠹，手自編緝，筐篋盈滿。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning and could compose; the family's old books were all damaged by worms—he personally collated them until baskets and cases were full.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning and could compose. The family's old books were worm-eaten; he personally collated them until baskets and cases overflowed.

sentences.zh: 梁初，以臨川王妃弟，故自征虜主簿遷右軍功曹，累遷太子洗馬，掌書記，侍講壽光殿。

translations.literal: Early in Liang, as brother to the Princess of Linchuan, he moved from Chief Clerk on the Pacifying Campaign staff to Army Controller in the Right Army, then to Crown Prince's Groom, in charge of records, lecturing in the Shouguang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Liang, as brother to the Princess of Linchuan, he moved from Chief Clerk on the Pacifying Campaign staff to Army Controller in the Right Army, then to Crown Prince's Groom in charge of records, lecturing in the Shouguang Hall.

sentences.zh: 及從兄孝綽等並以文藻見知，多預宴坐。

translations.literal: With his cousins Xiaochuo and others he was known for literary grace and often attended banquets.
translations.idiomatic: He and his cousins Xiaochuo and others were known for literary grace and often attended banquets.

sentences.zh: 受詔詠天泉池荷及采菱調，下筆即成。

translations.literal: Receiving edicts to compose on the lotus of the Tianquan Pool and on the melody of gathering water chestnuts, he finished as soon as the brush touched paper.
translations.idiomatic: Receiving edicts to compose on the lotus of the Tianquan Pool and on the melody of gathering water chestnuts, he finished as soon as the brush touched paper.

sentences.zh: 天監十年卒，臨終呼友人南陽劉之遴托以喪事從儉。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Tianjian he died; at the end he called his friend Liu Zhilin of Nanyang and entrusted him with funeral arrangements kept simple.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Tianjian he died; at the end he called his friend Liu Zhilin of Nanyang and entrusted him with keeping the funeral arrangements simple.

sentences.zh: 苞居官有能名，性和直，與人交，面折其非，退稱其美，士友咸以此嘆惜之。

translations.literal: Bao in office had a reputation for ability; his nature was upright and direct—in dealing with others he would rebuke their faults to their face and afterward praise their virtues; gentlemen and friends all sighed over this.
translations.idiomatic: Bao in office had a reputation for ability. Upright and direct by nature, in dealing with others he would rebuke their faults to their face and afterward praise their virtues; gentlemen and friends all sighed over this.

sentences.zh: 繪字士章，愃弟也。

translations.literal: Hui, courtesy name Shizhang, was Quan's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hui, courtesy name Shizhang, was Quan's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 初為齊高帝行參軍，帝歎曰：「劉公為不亡也。

translations.literal: At first he was Acting Army Controller under Emperor Gao of Qi; the emperor sighed: "Lord Liu is not dead after all."
translations.idiomatic: At first he served as Acting Army Controller under Emperor Gao of Qi; the emperor sighed: "Lord Liu is not dead after all."

sentences.zh: 」及豫章王嶷鎮江陵，繪為鎮西外兵參軍，以文義見禮。

translations.literal: When Prince of Yuzhang Diao garrisoned Jiangling, Hui was Army Controller on the Pacified West staff and was honored for literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yuzhang Diao garrisoned Jiangling, Hui served as Army Controller on the Pacified West staff and was honored for literary learning.

sentences.zh: 時琅邪王詡為功曹，以吏能自進，嶷謂僚佐曰：「吾雖不能得應嗣陳蕃，然合下自有二驥也。」

translations.literal: At the time Wang Xu of Langya was Merit Officer and advanced through administrative ability; Diao told his staff: "Though I cannot have Ying Shao or Chen Fan, below me I have two fine steeds."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wang Xu of Langya was Merit Officer and advanced through administrative ability. Diao told his staff: "Though I cannot have men like Ying Shao or Chen Fan, below me I have two fine steeds."

sentences.zh: 性通悟，出為南康相，郡人有姓賴，所居名穢裏，刺謁繪，繪戲嘲之曰：「君有何穢，而居穢裏？

translations.literal: By nature quick-witted, he went out as Administrator of Nankang; a man of the commandery surnamed Lai lived in a lane called Filthy Lane and came to pay a formal visit; Hui jested: "What filth do you have, that you dwell in Filthy Lane?"
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted by nature, he went out as Administrator of Nankang. A man of the commandery surnamed Lai lived in a lane called Filthy Lane and came to pay a formal visit. Hui jested: "What filth do you have, that you dwell in Filthy Lane?"

sentences.zh: 」此人應聲曰：「未審孔丘何闕，而居闕里。

translations.literal: The man answered on the spot: "I wonder what fault Confucius had, that he dwelt in Que Lane."
translations.idiomatic: The man answered on the spot: "I wonder what fault Confucius had, that he dwelt in Que Lane."

sentences.zh: 」繪默然不答，亦無忤意，歎其辯速。

translations.literal: Hui was silent and did not reply, nor showed offense, and admired his quick wit.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was silent and did not reply, nor showed any offense, and admired his quick wit.

sentences.zh: 後歷位中書郎，掌詔誥。

translations.literal: Later he held the post of Secretariat Gentleman, in charge of edicts and patents.
translations.idiomatic: Later he held the post of Secretariat Gentleman, in charge of edicts and patents of nobility.

sentences.zh: 敕助國子祭酒何胤撰修禮儀。

translations.literal: He was ordered to assist National University Libationer He Yin in compiling ritual regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to assist National University Libationer He Yin in compiling ritual regulations.

sentences.zh: 永明末，都下人士盛為文章談義，皆湊竟陵西邸，繪為後進領袖。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongming, gentlemen of the capital flourished in literary composition and discourses on meaning, all gathering at the Western Lodge of Jingling—Hui was leader among the younger generation.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yongming, gentlemen of the capital flourished in literary composition and discourses on meaning, all gathering at Jingling's Western Lodge—Hui led the younger generation.

sentences.zh: 時張融以言辭辯捷，周顒彌為清綺，而繪音采贍麗，雅有風則。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Rong was noted for eloquent, nimble speech, Zhou Yong especially for pure refinement, while Hui's tones were rich and beautiful, with elegant standards.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhang Rong was noted for eloquent, nimble speech and Zhou Yong especially for pure refinement, while Hui's style was rich and beautiful, with elegant standards.

sentences.zh: 時人為之語曰：「三人共宅夾清漳，張南周北劉中央。

translations.literal: People of the time made a saying: "Three men share a house flanking the clear Zhang—Zhang to the south, Zhou to the north, Liu in the center."
translations.idiomatic: People of the time made a rhyme: "Three men share a house flanking the clear Zhang—Zhang to the south, Zhou to the north, Liu in the center."

sentences.zh: 」言其處二人間也。

translations.literal: This meant he stood between the two men.
translations.idiomatic: This meant he stood between the two men.

sentences.zh: 魚復侯子響誅後，豫章王嶷欲求葬之，召繪為表言其事，繪須臾便成。

translations.literal: After Marquis of Yufu Zixiang was executed, Prince of Yuzhang Diao wished to have him buried and summoned Hui to draft a memorial on the matter—Hui finished in a moment.
translations.idiomatic: After Marquis of Yufu Zixiang was executed, Prince Yuzhang Diao wished to have him buried and summoned Hui to draft a memorial on the matter—Hui finished in a moment.

sentences.zh: 嶷歎曰：「禰衡何以過此。

translations.literal: Diao sighed: "How could Mi Heng surpass this?"
translations.idiomatic: Diao sighed: "How could Mi Heng surpass this?"

sentences.zh: 」唯足八字云：「提攜鞠養，俯見成人。

translations.literal: Only eight characters were added: "Raised and nurtured in your arms, I looked up and saw a grown man."
translations.idiomatic: He added only eight characters: "Raised and nurtured in your arms, I looked up and saw a grown man."

sentences.zh: 」後魏使至，繪以辭辯被敕接使。

translations.literal: Later an envoy from Wei arrived; Hui was ordered to receive the envoy for his eloquence.
translations.idiomatic: Later an envoy from Wei arrived; Hui was ordered to receive the envoy because of his eloquence.

sentences.zh: 事畢，當撰語辭。

translations.literal: When the business was done, he was to compose the diplomatic wording.
translations.idiomatic: When the business was done, he was to compose the diplomatic wording.

sentences.zh: 繪謂人曰：「無論潤色未易，但得我語亦難矣。」

translations.literal: Hui told people: "Never mind polishing—it is not easy; but even to get my wording is hard."
translations.idiomatic: Hui told people: "Never mind polishing the text—that is not easy; but even capturing my wording is hard."

sentences.zh: 及梁武起兵，朝廷以繪為雍州刺史，固讓不就。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang raised his army, the court appointed Hui Inspector of Yongzhou; he firmly declined and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang raised his army, the court appointed Hui Inspector of Yongzhou; he firmly declined and did not take office.

sentences.zh: 眾以朝廷昏亂，為之寒心。

translations.literal: The multitude, seeing the court's confusion, were chilled at heart for him.
translations.idiomatic: Many, seeing the court's confusion, were chilled at heart on his account.

sentences.zh: 繪終不受，乃改用張欣泰。

translations.literal: Hui in the end did not accept, and Zhang Xintai was appointed instead.
translations.idiomatic: Hui in the end did not accept, and Zhang Xintai was appointed instead.

sentences.zh: 轉繪建安王車騎長史，行府國事。

translations.literal: Hui was transferred to Chief Clerk on the Chariots and Cavalry staff of the Prince of Jian'an, acting on the prince's domain affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was transferred to Chief Clerk on the Chariots and Cavalry staff of the Prince of Jian'an, with authority over the prince's domain affairs.

sentences.zh: 及東昏見殺，城內遣繪及國子博士范雲等齎其首詣梁武帝於石頭。

translations.literal: When Donghun was killed, the city sent Hui and National University Erudite Fan Yun and others to carry his head to Emperor Wu of Liang at Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Donghun was killed, the city sent Hui and National University Erudite Fan Yun and others to carry his head to Emperor Wu of Liang at Shitou.

sentences.zh: 轉大司馬從事中郎，卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Army Controller in the Grand Marshal's staff and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Army Controller on the Grand Marshal's staff and died.

sentences.zh: 子孝綽。

translations.literal: His son Xiaochuo.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Liu Xiaochuo.

sentences.zh: 孝綽字孝綽，本名冉。

translations.literal: Xiaochuo, courtesy name Xiaochuo, original given name Ran.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiaochuo, courtesy name Xiaochuo, had the original given name Ran.

sentences.zh: 幼聰敏，七歲能屬文。

translations.literal: From childhood he was clever; at seven he could compose prose.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was clever; at seven he could compose prose.

sentences.zh: 舅齊中書郎王融深賞異之，與同載以適親友，號曰神童。

translations.literal: His uncle Wang Rong, Secretariat Gentleman of Qi, greatly admired and favored him, took him in the same carriage to visit kin and friends, and called him a divine child.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Wang Rong, Secretariat Gentleman of Qi, greatly admired him, took him in the same carriage to visit kin and friends, and called him a divine child.

sentences.zh: 融每曰：「天下文章若無我，當歸阿士。

translations.literal: Rong often said: "If there were no me in the world's literature, it would belong to A Shi."
translations.idiomatic: Rong often said: "If there were no me in the world's literature, it would belong to A Shi."

sentences.zh: 」阿士即孝綽小字也。

translations.literal: A Shi was Xiaochuo's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: A Shi was Xiaochuo's childhood name.

sentences.zh: 父繪，齊時掌詔誥，孝綽時年十四，繪常使代草之。

translations.literal: His father Hui in Qi times was in charge of edicts and patents; when Xiaochuo was fourteen, Hui often had him draft them.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hui in Qi times controlled edicts and patents; when Xiaochuo was fourteen, Hui often had him draft them in his place.

sentences.zh: 父党沈約、任昉、范雲等聞其名，命駕造焉，昉尤相賞好。

translations.literal: Shen Yue, Ren Fang, Fan Yun, and other friends of his father heard his name and ordered their carriages to visit him; Fang especially prized and befriended him.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yue, Ren Fang, Fan Yun, and other friends of his father heard his name and came to visit; Fang especially prized and befriended him.

sentences.zh: 範雲年長繪十餘歲，其子孝才與孝綽年並十四五。

translations.literal: Fan Yun was more than ten years older than Hui; his son Xiaocai and Xiaochuo were both fourteen or fifteen.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yun was more than ten years older than Hui; his son Xiaocai and Xiaochuo were both fourteen or fifteen.

sentences.zh: 及雲遇孝綽，便申伯季，乃命孝才拜之。

translations.literal: When Yun met Xiaochuo, he declared elder and younger brotherhood and ordered Xiaocai to bow to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yun met Xiaochuo, he declared elder and younger brotherhood and ordered Xiaocai to bow to him.

sentences.zh: 兼善草隸，自以書似父，乃變為別體。

translations.literal: He was also skilled in cursive and clerical script; thinking his writing resembled his father's, he changed to a different style.
translations.idiomatic: He was also skilled in cursive and clerical script; thinking his writing resembled his father's, he changed to a different style.

sentences.zh: 梁天監初，起家著作佐郎，為歸沐詩贈任昉，昉報曰：「彼美洛陽子，投我懷秋作，詎慰耋嗟人，徒深老夫托。

translations.literal: Early in Liang Tianjian he entered office as Assistant Editor in the Palace Library and presented a poem on returning home to bathe to Ren Fang; Fang replied: "That fair son of Luoyang sends me an autumn composition in his embrace—how could it comfort a man sighing in old age? It is only a deep trust from an old friend."
translations.idiomatic: Early in Liang Tianjian he entered office as Assistant Editor in the Palace Library and presented a poem on returning home to bathe to Ren Fang; Fang replied: "That fair son of Luoyang sends me an autumn piece in his embrace—how could it comfort a man sighing in old age? It is only a deep trust from an old friend."

sentences.zh: 直史兼褒貶，轄司專疾惡，九折多美疹，匪報庶良藥。

translations.literal: "Straight historian with praise and blame, the supervising office especially hates evil; nine bends bring many sores—no return, yet perhaps good medicine."
translations.idiomatic: "As straight historian with praise and blame, the supervising office especially hates evil; nine bends bring many sores—no return, yet perhaps good medicine."

sentences.zh: 」其為名流所重如此。

translations.literal: Such was the weight the leading men gave him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the weight the leading men gave him.

sentences.zh: 後遷兼尚書水部郎，奉啟陳謝。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to concurrent Director in the Ministry of Works' Water Bureau and submitted a memorial of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was transferred to concurrent Director in the Ministry of Works' Water Bureau and submitted a memorial of thanks.

sentences.zh: 手敕答曰：「美錦未可便制，簿領亦宜稍習。

translations.literal: An imperial note in the emperor's hand answered: "Fine brocade cannot be cut at once; ledgers too should be studied a little."
translations.idiomatic: An imperial note in the emperor's hand answered: "Fine brocade cannot be cut at once; ledgers too should be studied a little."

sentences.zh: 」頃之即真。

translations.literal: Before long he received regular appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he received regular appointment.

sentences.zh: 武帝時因宴幸，令沈約、任昉等言志賦詩，孝綽亦見引。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu was feasting on a tour of favor, he had Shen Yue, Ren Fang, and others speak their ambitions and compose poetry; Xiaochuo too was summoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu feasted on a tour of favor, he had Shen Yue, Ren Fang, and others speak their ambitions and compose poetry; Xiaochuo too was summoned.

sentences.zh: 嘗侍宴，於坐作詩七首，武帝覽其文，篇篇嗟賞，由是朝野改觀。

translations.literal: Once attending a feast, he composed seven poems in his seat; the emperor read each and sighed in admiration at every piece, and from this court and countryside changed their view of him.
translations.idiomatic: Once at a feast he composed seven poems in his seat. The emperor read each in turn and sighed in admiration at every one; from this court and countryside changed their view of him.

sentences.zh: 累遷秘書丞。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Palace Library Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Palace Library Director.

sentences.zh: 武帝謂舍人周舍云：「第一官當知用第一人。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu told Attendant Zhou She: "The first office should employ the first man."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu told Attendant Zhou She: "The first office should employ the first man."

sentences.zh: 」故以孝綽居此職。

translations.literal: Therefore Xiaochuo was placed in this post.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Xiaochuo was placed in this post.

sentences.zh: 後為太子僕，掌東宮管記。

translations.literal: Later he became Crown Prince's Steward, in charge of the Eastern Palace records.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became Crown Prince's Steward, in charge of the Eastern Palace records.

sentences.zh: 時昭明太子好士愛文，孝綽與陳郡殷芸、吳郡陸倕、琅邪王筠、彭城到洽等同見禮。

translations.literal: At the time Crown Prince Zhaoming loved scholars and cherished literature; Xiaochuo, Yin Yun of Chen commandery, Lu Chun of Wu commandery, Wang Jun of Langya, and Dao Qia of Pengcheng were alike honored.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Crown Prince Zhaoming loved scholars and cherished literature. Xiaochuo, Yin Yun of Chen, Lu Chun of Wu, Wang Jun of Langya, and Dao Qia of Pengcheng were all honored alike.

sentences.zh: 太子起樂賢堂，乃使先圖孝綽。

translations.literal: The crown prince raised the Hall of Cherishing Worthies and first had Xiaochuo's portrait painted.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince raised the Hall of Cherishing Worthies and first had Xiaochuo's portrait painted.

sentences.zh: 太子文章，群才咸欲撰錄，太子獨使孝綽集而序之。

translations.literal: The crown prince's writings—all the talented wished to compile and record them—but the crown prince had Xiaochuo alone collect and arrange them.
translations.idiomatic: For the crown prince's writings, all the talented wished to compile and record them, but the crown prince had Xiaochuo alone collect and arrange them.

sentences.zh: 遷兼廷尉卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to concurrent Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to concurrent Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 初，孝綽與到溉兄弟甚狎，溉少孤，宅近僧寺，孝綽往溉許，適見黃臥具，孝綽謂僧物色也，撫手笑。

translations.literal: Earlier Xiaochuo had been very intimate with the brothers Dao Gai; Gai was orphaned young and lived near a Buddhist temple; when Xiaochuo went to Gai's place he happened to see yellow bedding and, thinking it monastic goods, clapped his hands and laughed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xiaochuo had been very close to the brothers Dao Gai. Gai was orphaned young and lived near a monastery; when Xiaochuo visited and saw yellow bedding, he thought it monastic property and laughed aloud.

sentences.zh: 溉知其旨，奮拳擊之，傷口而去。

translations.literal: Gai knew his meaning and struck out with his fist, wounding his mouth before leaving.
translations.idiomatic: Gai knew his meaning and struck out with his fist, wounding Xiaochuo's mouth before leaving.

sentences.zh: 又與洽同遊東宮，孝綽自以才優於洽，每於宴坐嗤鄙其文，洽深銜之。

translations.literal: He also toured the Eastern Palace with Qia; Xiaochuo thought himself more talented than Qia and at banquets often ridiculed his writing; Qia deeply resented it.
translations.idiomatic: He also toured the Eastern Palace with Qia. Xiaochuo thought himself the better writer and at banquets often ridiculed Qia's compositions; Qia deeply resented it.

sentences.zh: 及孝綽為廷尉，攜妾入廷尉，其母猶停私宅。

translations.literal: When Xiaochuo became Minister of Justice, he brought a concubine into the court; his mother still remained in a private residence.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaochuo became Minister of Justice, he brought a concubine into the court offices; his mother still remained in a private residence.

sentences.zh: 洽尋為御史中丞，遣令史劾奏之，云：「攜少妹于華省，棄老母於下宅。

translations.literal: Qia soon became Imperial Censor; he sent a clerk to impeach him, saying: "He keeps a young sister in the splendid office and abandons his old mother in a lowly dwelling."
translations.idiomatic: Qia soon became Imperial Censor and sent a clerk to impeach him, saying: "He keeps a young sister in the splendid office and abandons his old mother in a lowly dwelling."

sentences.zh: 」武帝為隱其惡，改妹字為姝。

translations.literal: The emperor concealed his fault and changed the character for sister to another meaning.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor concealed his fault and changed the character for sister to another meaning in the memorial.

sentences.zh: 孝綽坐免官。

translations.literal: Xiaochuo was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaochuo was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 諸弟時隨蕃皆在荊、雍，乃與書論共洽不平者十事，其辭皆訴到氏。

translations.literal: His younger brothers at the time were all with the princes in Jing and Yong; he wrote to them discussing ten points of grievance against Qia, the wording all accusing the Dao clan.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers were then all with the princes in Jing and Yong. He wrote to them setting forth ten grievances against Qia, the wording throughout accusing the Dao clan.

sentences.zh: 又寫別本封至東宮，昭明太子命焚之，不開視。

translations.literal: He also copied a separate version sealed and sent to the Eastern Palace; Crown Prince Zhaoming ordered it burned unopened.
