translations.idiomatic: He also copied a separate version, sealed it, and sent it to the Eastern Palace; Crown Prince Zhaoming ordered it burned unopened.

sentences.zh: 孝綽免職後，武帝數使僕射徐勉宣旨慰撫之，每朝宴常預焉。

translations.literal: After Xiaochuo was dismissed, Emperor Wu several times sent Vice Director Xu Mian with imperial words to comfort him; he was often present at morning feasts.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiaochuo was dismissed, Emperor Wu several times sent Vice Director Xu Mian with imperial words to comfort him, and he was often present at morning feasts.

sentences.zh: 及武帝為籍田詩，又使勉先示孝綽。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu composed a poem on the plowing ceremony, he again had Mian show it first to Xiaochuo.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu composed a poem on the plowing ceremony, he again had Mian show it first to Xiaochuo.

sentences.zh: 時奉詔作者數十人，帝以孝綽詩工，即日起為西中郎湘東王諮議參軍。

translations.literal: At the time dozens composed on imperial command; the emperor thought Xiaochuo's poetry finest and that very day appointed him Army Controller on the Western Army staff of Prince Xiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens composed on imperial command at the time. The emperor judged Xiaochuo's poetry the finest and that very day appointed him Army Controller on Prince Xiangdong's Western Army staff.

sentences.zh: 遷黃門侍郎、尚書吏部郎，坐受人絹一束，為餉者所訟，左遷信威臨賀王長史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Palace Attendant and Director of the Ministry of Personnel; for accepting a gift of one bolt of silk from a presenter who sued him, he was demoted to Chief Clerk to Prince Linhe of Trustworthy Might.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Palace Attendant and Director of the Ministry of Personnel. When he accepted one bolt of silk as a gift, the giver sued him, and he was demoted to Chief Clerk to Prince Linhe of Trustworthy Might.

sentences.zh: 晚年忽忽不得志，後為秘書監。

translations.literal: In his later years he was suddenly restless and unfulfilled; later he became Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he was suddenly restless and unfulfilled; later he became Director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 初，孝綽居母憂，冬月飲冷水，因得冷癖，以大同五年卒官，年五十九。

translations.literal: Earlier, while in mourning for his mother, in winter he drank cold water and contracted a chronic cold ailment; in the fifth year of Datong he died in office at age fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while mourning his mother, he drank cold water in winter and contracted a chronic cold ailment. In the fifth year of Datong he died in office at fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 孝綽少有盛名，而仗氣負才，多所陵忽。

translations.literal: Xiaochuo from youth had great fame, yet relied on his spirit and prized his talent, looking down on many.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaochuo from youth had great fame, yet relied on his spirit and prized his talent, looking down on many.

sentences.zh: 有不合意，極言詆訾。

translations.literal: When something did not please him, he slandered it to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: When something did not please him, he slandered it to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 領軍臧盾、太府卿沈僧畟等並被時遇，孝綽尤輕之。

translations.literal: Army Commander Zang Dun, Minister of the Imperial Storehouse Shen Sengbi, and others were all favored by the times; Xiaochuo especially despised them.
translations.idiomatic: Army Commander Zang Dun, Minister of the Imperial Storehouse Shen Sengbi, and others were all favored by the times, yet Xiaochuo especially despised them.

sentences.zh: 每于朝集會同，處公卿間無所與語，反呼騶卒訪道途間事，由此多忤於物，前後五免。

translations.literal: At every court assembly among the ministers he spoke with no one, but instead called grooms to ask about affairs on the roads; thereby he often gave offense and was dismissed five times in all.
translations.idiomatic: At every court assembly he spoke with none of the ministers, but instead called grooms to ask about affairs on the roads. Thereby he often gave offense and was dismissed five times in all.

sentences.zh: 孝綽辭藻為後進所宗，時重其文，每作一篇，朝成暮遍，好事者咸誦傳寫，流聞河朔，亭苑柱壁莫不題之。

translations.literal: Xiaochuo's literary style was revered by the younger generation; the age prized his writing—each piece he made was known by morning and spread by evening; enthusiasts all recited and copied it, reaching north of the Yellow River; pavilion gardens' pillars and walls were all inscribed with it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaochuo's literary style was revered by the younger generation. The age prized his writing: each new piece was known by morning and copied by evening; enthusiasts recited it far north of the Yellow River, and pavilion pillars and garden walls were inscribed with his lines.

sentences.zh: 文集數十萬言，行于時。

translations.literal: His collected works ran to several hundred thousand words and circulated in his time.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to several hundred thousand words and circulated in his time.

sentences.zh: 兄弟及群從子侄當時有七十人，並能屬文，近古未之有也。

translations.literal: Brothers and cousins and nephews at the time numbered seventy, all able to compose—unmatched in recent antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Brothers, cousins, and nephews at the time numbered seventy, all able to compose—something unmatched in recent antiquity.

sentences.zh: 其三妹，一適琅邪王叔英，一適吳郡張嵊，一適東海徐悱，並有才學。

translations.literal: Of his three younger sisters, one married Wang Shuying of Langya, one Zhang Song of Wu commandery, one Xu Fei of Donghai—all had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Of his three younger sisters, one married Wang Shuying of Langya, one Zhang Song of Wu commandery, and one Xu Fei of Donghai—all were accomplished in letters.

sentences.zh: 悱妻文尤清拔，所謂劉三娘者也。

translations.literal: Fei's wife's writing was especially pure and striking—the so-called Lady Liu the Third.
translations.idiomatic: Fei's wife's writing was especially pure and striking—the so-called Lady Liu the Third.

sentences.zh: 悱為晉安郡卒，喪還建鄴，妻為祭文，辭甚悽愴。

translations.literal: Fei died as Administrator of Jin'an; when the coffin returned to Jianye, his wife composed a sacrificial text of very moving words.
translations.idiomatic: Fei died as Administrator of Jin'an. When the coffin returned to Jianye, his wife composed a sacrificial text of very moving words.

sentences.zh: 悱父勉本欲為哀辭，及見此文，乃閣筆。

translations.literal: Fei's father Mian had intended to compose a lament, but on seeing this text he laid down his brush.
translations.idiomatic: Fei's father Mian had intended to compose a lament, but on seeing this text he laid down his brush.

sentences.zh: 孝綽子諒字求信，小名春。

translations.literal: Xiaochuo's son Liang, courtesy name Qiuxin, childhood name Chun.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaochuo's son Liang, courtesy name Qiuxin, childhood name Chun.

sentences.zh: 少好學，有文才，尤悉晉代故事，時人號曰：「皮裏晉書」。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning and had literary talent, especially versed in Jin-dynasty stories; people of the time called him "the Jin History in a skin."
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning and had literary talent, especially versed in Jin-dynasty stories; contemporaries called him "the Jin History wrapped in skin."

sentences.zh: 位中書宣城王記室，為湘東王所善。

translations.literal: He reached Secretariat Recorder on the staff of the Prince of Xuancheng and was favored by Prince Xiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Secretariat Recorder on the staff of the Prince of Xuancheng and was favored by Prince Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 王嘗游江濱，歎秋望之美。

translations.literal: The prince once toured the riverbank, sighing at the beauty of the autumn view.
translations.idiomatic: The prince once toured the riverbank, sighing at the beauty of the autumn view.

sentences.zh: 諒對曰：「今日可謂'帝子降於北渚'。

translations.literal: Liang replied: "Today one may say 'the emperor's son descends to the northern islet.'"
translations.idiomatic: Liang replied: "Today one may say 'the emperor's son descends to the northern islet.'"

sentences.zh: 」王有目疾，以為刺己。

translations.literal: The prince had an eye ailment and thought it a barb at himself.
translations.idiomatic: The prince had an eye ailment and thought it a barb at himself.

sentences.zh: 應曰：「卿言'目眇眇以愁予'邪？

translations.literal: He answered: "Do you mean 'the eyes dim dim grieve me'?"
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Do you mean 'the eyes dim dim grieve me'?"

sentences.zh: 」從此嫌之。

translations.literal: From this the prince bore a grudge against him.
translations.idiomatic: From this the prince bore a grudge against him.

sentences.zh: 孝綽弟潛字孝儀，幼孤，與諸兄弟相勖以學，並工屬文。

translations.literal: Xiaochuo's younger brother Qian, courtesy name Xiaoyi, was orphaned young; with his brothers he urged one another in study, and all were skilled at composition.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaochuo's younger brother Liu Qian, courtesy name Xiaoyi, was orphaned young; with his brothers he urged one another in study, and all were skilled at composition.

sentences.zh: 孝綽嘗云：「三筆六詩」，三即孝儀，六謂孝威也。

translations.literal: Xiaochuo once said: "Three brushes and six poems"—the three meant Xiaoyi, the six meant Xiaowei.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaochuo once said, "Three brushes and six poems"—the three meant Xiaoyi, the six Xiaowei.

sentences.zh: 孝儀為人寬厚，內行尤篤。

translations.literal: Xiaoyi was generous in bearing and especially devoted in inner conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyi was generous in bearing and especially devoted in inner conduct.

sentences.zh: 第二兄孝熊早卒，孝儀奉寡嫂甚謹，家內巨細必先諮決，與妻子朝夕供事，未嘗失禮，時人以此稱之。

translations.literal: His second elder brother Xiaoxiong died early; Xiaoyi served his widowed sister-in-law with great respect, and in household matters great or small he always consulted her first; with wife and children he attended her morning and evening without ever failing in ritual—people of the time praised this.
translations.idiomatic: His second elder brother Xiaoxiong died early. Xiaoyi served his widowed sister-in-law with scrupulous respect; in household matters great or small he always consulted her first. With wife and children he attended her morning and evening without ever failing in ritual, and people of the time praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 有文集二十卷行於世。

translations.literal: He left a collected works in twenty juan circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected works in twenty juan circulating in the world.

sentences.zh: 第五弟孝勝，位尚書右丞、兼散騎常侍。

translations.literal: The fifth younger brother Xiaosheng held the posts of Right Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing and concurrent Privy Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth younger brother Xiaosheng held the posts of Right Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing and concurrent Privy Attendant.

sentences.zh: 聘魏還，為安西武陵王紀長史、蜀郡太守。

translations.literal: After an embassy to Wei he returned and became Chief Clerk to Prince Anxi of Wuling and Administrator of Shujun.
translations.idiomatic: After an embassy to Wei he returned and became Chief Clerk to Prince Anxi of Wuling and Administrator of Shujun.

sentences.zh: 紀僭號於蜀，以為尚書僕射。

translations.literal: When Ji usurped the title in Shu, he was made Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji usurped the title in Shu, he was made Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 隨紀出峽口，兵敗被執。

translations.literal: Following Ji out of the gorge mouth, the army was defeated and he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Following Ji out of the gorge mouth, the army was defeated and he was captured.

sentences.zh: 元帝宥之，以為司徒右長史。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan pardoned him and appointed him Right Chief Clerk of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan pardoned him and appointed him Right Chief Clerk of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 第六弟孝威，氣調爽逸，風儀俊舉。

translations.literal: The sixth younger brother Xiaowei had a spirited, free manner and handsome bearing.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth younger brother Xiaowei had a spirited, free manner and handsome bearing.

sentences.zh: 初為安北晉安王法曹，後為太子洗馬，中舍人，庶子，率更令，並掌管記。

translations.literal: At first he was Legal Officer on the Pacified North staff of Prince Jin'an; later Crown Prince's Groom, Attendant, Palace Son, Director of the Directorate of Astronomy—all concurrently in charge of records.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was Legal Officer on Prince Jin'an's Pacified North staff; later he served as Crown Prince's Groom, Attendant, Palace Son, and Director of the Directorate of Astronomy, in each post keeping charge of records.

sentences.zh: 大同中，白雀集東宮，孝威上頌甚美。

translations.literal: In Datong, white sparrows gathered at the Eastern Palace; Xiaowei submitted a eulogy of great beauty.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong, white sparrows gathered at the Eastern Palace; Xiaowei submitted a eulogy of great beauty.

sentences.zh: 太清中，遷中庶子，兼通事舍人。

translations.literal: In Taiqing he was promoted to Palace Attendant and concurrent Attendant for Current Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiqing he was promoted to Palace Attendant and concurrent Attendant for Current Affairs.

sentences.zh: 及侯景寇亂，隨司州刺史柳仲禮至安陸，卒。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing raided in disorder, he followed Inspector of Sizhou Liu Zhongli to Anyang and died there.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing raided in disorder, he followed Inspector of Sizhou Liu Zhongli to Anyang and died there.

sentences.zh: 第七弟孝先，位武陵王主簿，與兄孝勝俱隨紀軍出峽口。

translations.literal: The seventh younger brother Xiaoxian was Chief Clerk to Prince Wuling and followed his brother Xiaosheng with Ji's army out of the gorge mouth.
translations.idiomatic: The seventh younger brother Xiaoxian served as Chief Clerk to Prince Wuling and, with his brother Xiaosheng, followed Ji's army out of the gorge mouth.

sentences.zh: 兵敗，元帝以為黃門郎，遷侍中。

translations.literal: The army was defeated; Emperor Yuan made him Palace Attendant and promoted him to Palace Attendant in regular appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The army was defeated; Emperor Yuan made him Palace Attendant and promoted him to Palace Attendant in regular appointment.

sentences.zh: 瑱字士溫，繪弟也。

translations.literal: Zhen, courtesy name Shiwen, was Hui's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhen, courtesy name Shiwen, was Hui's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 少有行業，文藻、篆隸、丹青並為當世所稱。

translations.literal: From youth he had good conduct; literature, seal script, clerical script, and painting were all acclaimed in his age.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he had good conduct; literature, seal script, clerical script, and painting were all acclaimed in his age.

sentences.zh: 時有滎陽毛惠遠善畫馬，瑱善畫婦人，並為當世第一。

translations.literal: At the time Mao Huiyuan of Xingyang was skilled at painting horses, Zhen at painting women—both were first in the age.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Mao Huiyuan of Xingyang was skilled at painting horses and Zhen at painting women—each was first in the age.

sentences.zh: 瑱妹為齊鄱陽王妃，伉儷甚篤。

translations.literal: Zhen's younger sister was consort to the Princess of Poyang of Qi; husband and wife were deeply devoted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's younger sister was consort to the Princess of Poyang of Qi; husband and wife were deeply devoted.

sentences.zh: 王為齊明帝所誅，妃追傷遂成痼疾，醫所不療。

translations.literal: The prince was executed by Emperor Ming of Qi; the consort grieved and became chronically ill, beyond physicians' cure.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was executed by Emperor Ming of Qi; the consort grieved until she fell into chronic illness that physicians could not cure.

sentences.zh: 有陳郡殷蒨善寫人面，與真不別，瑱令蒨畫王形像，並圖王平生所寵姬共照鏡狀，如欲偶寢。

translations.literal: Yin Qian of Chen commandery was skilled at painting human faces indistinguishable from life; Zhen had Qian paint the prince's likeness together with the prince's favorite concubines gazing in a mirror as if about to share the bed.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Qian of Chen commandery could paint human faces indistinguishable from life. Zhen had Qian paint the prince's likeness together with the prince's favorite concubines gazing in a mirror, as if about to share the bed.

sentences.zh: 瑱乃密使媼奶示妃，妃視畫仍唾之，因罵云：「故宜其早死」。

translations.literal: Zhen secretly had a nurse show the consort; she looked at the painting and spat at it, cursing: "So it was right that he died early."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen secretly had a nurse show the consort the painting. She looked at it and spat, cursing: "So it was right that he died early."

sentences.zh: 於是恩情即歇，病亦除差。

translations.literal: Thereupon affection ceased and the illness was cured.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon affection ceased and the illness was cured.

sentences.zh: 此姬亦被廢苦，因即以此畫焚之。

translations.literal: This concubine too had suffered in disgrace and therefore burned the painting.
translations.idiomatic: This concubine too had suffered in disgrace and therefore burned the painting.

sentences.zh: 瑱仕齊，曆尚書吏部郎，義興太守。

translations.literal: Zhen served Qi, holding posts as Director in the Ministry of Personnel and Administrator of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen served Qi, holding posts as Director in the Ministry of Personnel and Administrator of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 先繪卒。

translations.literal: He died before Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He died before Hui.

sentences.zh: 論曰：當泰始之際，二殷去就不同，原始要終，各以名節自立。

translations.literal: The judgment says: At the time of Taishi, the two Yins chose differently in going and staying; tracing origin and seeking end, each established himself by reputation and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: The judgment says: At the time of Taishi, the two Yins chose differently in going and staying; tracing origin and seeking end, each stood on reputation and integrity.

sentences.zh: 孝祖翫敵而亡，蓋其宜也。

translations.literal: Xiaozu treated the enemy lightly and perished—perhaps this was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozu treated the enemy lightly and died for it—perhaps that was only fitting.

sentences.zh: 劉勉出征久撫，所在流譽，行己之節，赴蹈為期，雖古之忠烈，亦何以加此。

translations.literal: Liu Mian on campaigns long pacified regions; wherever he went praise spread; his standard of personal conduct and keeping pledged word as his term—even ancient loyal martyrs, how could they surpass this?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian on long campaigns pacified the regions he held; wherever he went praise followed; in personal conduct he kept his pledged word as his bond—even the loyal martyrs of old could hardly have surpassed this.

sentences.zh: 悛至性過人，繪辭義克舉，諸子各擅雕龍，當年方駕，文采之盛，殆難繼乎。

translations.literal: Juan's supreme nature surpassed others; Hui fully achieved literary meaning; the sons each excelled in literary carving; in their age they matched chariots abreast; the brilliance of their writing perhaps can hardly be continued.
translations.idiomatic: Juan's filial nature surpassed others; Hui fully achieved literary excellence; the sons each excelled in polished writing; in their day they were equals abreast; such brilliance of prose can hardly be matched again.

sentences.zh: 孝綽中冓為尤，可謂人而無儀者矣。

translations.literal: Xiaochuo's incest was especially vile—he may be called a man without propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaochuo's incest was especially vile—he may truly be called a man without decency.
